[PROJECT NAME]

A team of agents that reviews a pull request. One plans the review, calls specialist reviewers, spawns extra workers for large changes, and waits for a person before posting anything.

[REPOSITORY LINK] [DEMO RECORDING LINK]

The question

Multi-agent systems are easy to build and hard to justify. This project asks one thing: does splitting a code review across several agents find more real bugs than a single agent, and what does it cost in money and time?

To answer it, [NUMBER] pull requests were prepared with known bugs planted in them, and each version of the reviewer was scored on how many it found.

How a review runs

{{note}}

Pull request
Orchestrator: reads the diff, plans the review

Called: three standing specialists

Bug reviewer
logic errors and edge cases
Security reviewer
its own service, called over A2A
Test reviewer
runs the tests in a sandbox

Spawned: one temporary worker per file, only for large changes

{{w.label}}
Verifier: drops weak findings
A person approves, edits or rejects
Comments posted
